title: Secure and dock a gel-casting cassette
instruction: Close both green pressure cams to secure the aligned glass plates. Lift the cassette from its alignment cradle, hold the clear stand lever open, and place the cassette on the gray sealing pad. Release the lever onto the tall plate and withdraw both grippers, leaving the assembly upright and stable.
context: Laboratory staff assemble a plate cassette and secure it on a casting stand before preparing a vertical polyacrylamide gel. This task covers the mechanical preparation: retain two aligned plates, transfer them without losing their alignment, and dock the cassette under a spring-return pressure clip. Liquid handling, polymerization, comb insertion and electrophoresis are outside its scope.
setup: Use the station scene with no object jitter. Coordinates are metres: x forward from the line through the arm bases, y left, z up; the table top is z=0.7475. The green polymer frame origin is (0.300,0.000,0.7385); its upright posts are 15 by 10 by 69 mm, centred at frame-local y=-55.5 and +55.5 mm, and its two side pressure cams start at -100 and +100 degrees. A clear rear glass plate, 101 mm wide by 82 mm tall by 3 mm thick, and a clear front plate, 101 by 73 by 3 mm, stand independently inside the frame. Two bonded spacer strips on the rear plate define the nominal 1 mm cavity. Plate centres in frame coordinates are (0,0,0.053) and (0.004,0,0.0485); both glass bottoms lie at local z=0.012. A fixed visible gray alignment cradle shares the initial frame origin: a 14 by 105 by 3 mm pad supports the bottoms and two slim front guides rise to local z=0.050 with 0.05 mm nominal face clearance. Visible 2.5 mm-high collars surround both frame feet with 0.05 mm clearance, bracing translation and yaw while leaving straight-up extraction free. The frame rear rails support the rear plate. Cam closure uses one gripper at a time; the fixed jig supplies frame support. The cam pusher approaches at a 33 mm TCP height offset above the pivot to clear the upper hinge ear, then retreats 20 mm horizontally along the measured cam normal before rising 70 mm. The current recorded full scripted demonstration succeeds from this deterministic reset (seed=None, zero object jitter). The clamped cassette must be lifted at least 45 mm clear of the jig; the controller lifts 140 mm over 4 seconds to cross above the full casting stand. The separate transparent polymer stand origin is (0.160,0.000,0.7475); its nominal envelope is 82 by 151 by 108 mm. A gray rigid rubber sealing pad, 14 by 105 by 3 mm, is installed at stand-local (0.002,0,0.0105). Its clear spring-return lever starts closed at zero degrees. Frame and stand are both rotated 180 degrees about z so their fronts face the robot. Plates, frame and stand are dynamic; only the cradle is fixed. No glass-to-frame or cassette-to-stand attachment is present. Refined stand support: four clear rear pads at local y=+/-38 mm and z=19/81 mm have 6 by 8 mm contact faces at x=-12.3 mm, leaving 0.3 mm nominal insertion clearance to collidable rear frame ribs at x=-12 mm. The visible rear ribs and matching collision proxies have an 88 mm centred span (ends at y=+/-44 mm), covering support faces through +/-41 mm while clearing the side-post grasp corridor. Low open-top foot guides have 0.3 mm lateral clearance. These are designed approximations, not manufacturer-measured fit. The nominal straight cassette path intersects the existing angled stand lever. The checked assembly approach holds the lever at or beyond -82 degrees, maintains a 2 mm forward cassette offset from 140 to 20 mm above seating, blends to zero offset by 8 mm, aligns the measured frame there for 3 seconds, lowers with pose feedback over 3 seconds, and allows 2 seconds to settle. The controller guards the lever opening throughout and refuses to release the carrying gripper unless measured docking geometry passes. Whole-assembly straight-up removal is outside the verified scope.
scoring: End-of-episode score, with one full second of pose qualification followed by an additional 3-second success hold. Any recorded fall of a frame, plate or stand origin more than 25 mm below the table makes the score zero. Otherwise the plates must be aligned: each plate-origin error from its intended frame-relative position less than 2 mm, each plate/frame angular difference less than 4 degrees, each of four sampled cavity gaps strictly within 1.00 +/- 0.25 mm, and each of four sampled bottom heights within 0.5 mm of the intended sealing level. Misalignment scores zero. A cam is closed strictly between -1 and +4 degrees on the left, or -4 and +1 on the right; each closed cam earns 0.15 only after that cam was observed more than 60 degrees open. Docking earns 0.60 only after both opening observations and a frame lift more than 25 mm: both cams closed, aligned glass, frame/stand horizontal origin error below 2.5 mm, vertical origin error below 0.6 mm, and relative orientation error below 3 degrees. Docking also requires four rear-rib/support clearances between -0.15 and +1.0 mm, absolute lateral frame offset at most 0.7 mm, and actual glass-bottom samples within 0.5 mm of the stand gasket plane. The top clip counts closed only with angle within 6 degrees of zero and transformed pressure-pad bottom samples within 0.5 mm of the tall plate top and within the stated 3 mm centring tolerance across its thickness. Docking plus this closed-clip check and stand within 5 degrees of upright earns 0.90. These surface checks establish geometric proximity, not contact force. Full success additionally requires both tool-centre points more than 145 mm from stand-local (0,0,0.060), no violation, and pose-based settling. For the frame, rear plate, front plate and stand, maximum pairwise position diameter must be at most 0.2 mm and normalized-quaternion geodesic diameter at most 0.2 degrees. Each of the two cam angles and the clip angle must span at most 0.5 degrees. Coarse raw-velocity guards reject any body at or above 50 mm/s or 2 rad/s. Qualification begins only while alignment, docking, closed clip, upright stand and hand clearance pass; it needs a full second of samples (21 at 20 Hz, using the actual control timestep). Candidate history expands through the additional 3-second framework hold, capped at 4 seconds, so slow cumulative drift cannot pass separate short windows. Gate loss, missing or invalid readings, excursions and coarse-motion violations clear qualification; reset clears all history. This measures settling within pose bounds, not zero reported velocity. The framework returns 1.00 for success; the partial score function is capped at 0.90. TCP clearance does not prove absence of all-link contact. The scorer does not measure sealing pressure, liquid leakage or continuous retention during transfer.
reset_notes: Restore the frame and stand to the stated marked poses, set the side cams to -100 and +100 degrees and the top lever to zero, and place the independent plates upright with their bottoms aligned on the preparation cradle. Clear the opening, transport, violation and success-hold history. The simulator reset restores this prepared arrangement; robot disassembly is not part of the task. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Reference-informed rigid-body simulation, not manufacturer CAD. Nominal geometry, masses, friction, spring detents and gripper contact patches; glass and rubber do not deform. No fluid, leakage, fracture or verified seal. Plates remain independent, with no attachment joints or post-reset pose corrections. Offset insertion is demonstrated for one fixed reset; straight-up removal is obstructed. Generalization and strict bimanual necessity are untested.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 in one 2,400-step trial (20 Hz); session-expiry recoveries occurred. Scripted demo: 1.0 in 1,413 steps (70.65 simulated seconds), within the same limit. Source-matched results and limitations are documented in README.md.
